content.comment_body: Hello! I need to connect a shaft encoder to a [product_name] ([version_no]). Unfortunately, my encoder output is NPN. I tried following the sketch from the installation guide ([url] -> Figure 4 NPN, White example). Instead of the trigger, I connected it directly to the [product_name] input. I used 2.7kΩ resistors and set V1 and V2 to 24V. This setup worked for a few hours, but after changing some wiring, I no longer get a signal. Could someone help me with these points: - Is my approach fundamentally flawed, or can it work with some adjustments? - How do I determine the correct resistor values? - How can I check if the encoder's transistor has been damaged? Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is trying to interface an NPN shaft encoder with a [product_name] ([version_no]) and faces issues with signal loss after modifying wiring. The main concerns are uncertainty about proper connection procedures, selecting appropriate resistor values, and diagnosing possible hardware damage. This highlights the need for clearer documentation on connecting third-party components.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking precise advice on connecting an NPN encoder to a [product_name] ([version_no]), guidance for choosing suitable resistor values, and troubleshooting steps to identify any damage to the encoder.
